description: In validate_stmt, when Tag('comparator') is found, the code does: if let Some(Form::Str(name)) = iter.peek() { check name } ; iter.next() (consume name). If the token after :comparator is NOT a Str (e.g. a malformed script with :comparator :something), iter.peek() does not match the if-let, the comparator name is not consumed by that branch, but then iter.next() in the else path still executes, consuming whatever token follows -- potentially skipping a valid form. On closer reading: the code does iter.next() unconditionally after the if-let block to 'consume the name (or whatever follows the tag)'. This means a :comparator tag with no following string SILENTLY drops the next token. For malformed scripts this is harmless (compile fails elsewhere), but the comment 'or whatever follows the tag' is a yellow flag.
title: sieve: validate_stmt comparator check does not consume name token when peek finds non-Str
